provenance: Opus 5.5 subscription CLI draft with host review/repairs, source restrictions and execution verification.

draft_notes.explanation:
The constructor uses a background (7), one 4-connected red blob (2), scattered single dots (8), and a full wall line (9) on one edge. The row or column next to the wall is always cleared to 7.

For each input dot, it collects the set of 4-neighbour colours that are in {2,7}. Scenes are rejected when that set is empty or contains both colours. A dot whose neighbours include red becomes red. Every other dot paints one extra dot on the adjacent cell toward the wall. The twin check rejects a scene if that cell is already a dot.

The wall side is a per-pair latent chosen at random by the generator, so it cannot come from d4. The emitted program finds it directly in visible coordinates: it is the edge whose whole row or column is palette[9]. That edge becomes a step vector (dy, dx), so the motion is written natively as up, down, left or right, with no rotation wrappers.

Colour roles are fixed constants: palette[7], palette[2], palette[8] and palette[9]. The program follows the archived solver's classification, which counts red vs background 4-neighbours with n_red > n_bg. Within the generator's domain this matches the generator's set test exactly, because red and background never both occur around a dot. Extensions are read from the input grid, as in the generator. A dot paints its neighbour only if that cell is in bounds and is background. In the domain this always holds, since the cleared line beside the wall guarantees it.

d4 needs no specialization, because the wall is detected per grid. Rectangular grids are handled by using separate H and W.
draft_notes.limitations:
Neither the factory nor the emitted program has been run, by me or by any test; acceptance rests entirely on the host's verification.

Outside the constructor's domain, two cases are handled by fallbacks rather than by the puzzle:
- Ambiguous dots, with both red and background neighbours or neither, use the archived majority rule (n_red > n_bg, so ties extend). The generator rejects such scenes, so this tie-break is not part of the intended rule.
- If no edge, or more than one edge, is entirely wall-coloured, the program falls back to the edge with the most wall cells. Such scenes cannot be produced.

The generator only makes square grids from 7x7 to 14x14. Rectangular support follows the same logic but has no generator coverage.

No constructor defects were found that affect the answer:
- Negative indices such as grid[-1] could appear in the slide step in principle. They are unreachable, because the line next to the wall is cleared to 7 after the dots are placed.
- The approved fixtures match the uniform rule as I read them.
